preamble:
Focus: databases and distributed systems, supported by useful Linux foundations.
Continue PostgreSQL now; bring in Linux observations as needed, then study SQLite. Return for deeper
Linux/container work before progressing through networking, Valkey, DuckDB, object storage, NATS and etcd.

The Go follow-ups are **optional project choices**, not extra course requirements. Pick one after
the relevant topic, using earlier lessons where helpful. Aim for **30–60 minutes in 2–4 short sessions**
with supplied setup: one mechanism, one failure or race, and one result to verify. These are planning
estimates, not tested timings. Setup-heavy branches assume their labs are already ready.

Keep projects to tiny datasets and a few local processes. Extend supplied Go fixtures rather than
building complete platforms. Early projects exercise local boundaries used by distributed systems;
later ones connect services. They do not establish independent-machine fault tolerance.

Discuss the approach and scope before creating a selected project. Use Go for these follow-ups,
including PostgreSQL projects; this does not change the existing pgcoach lesson-script convention.
All projects below are proposals, not claims of authored or validated exercises.

topics.title: Linux foundations and resource management
topics.tool: Linux CLI tools expose processes, files, memory, sockets and isolation.
topics.goals: Study ownership, lifetime, resource budgets and namespace views; learn to connect symptoms to scoped evidence. Use foundations alongside databases and deeper resource work afterward. 44-lesson v2 proposal.
topics.diagram:
client -> worker -> files / sockets
            |
         CPU + memory budget

followups.title: Bounded fan-out
followups.description: cap a supplied Go launcher's concurrency; verify useful progress and complete child cleanup.

followups.title: Pipe backpressure
followups.description: pause a Go consumer; observe its producer stall and recover without unbounded buffering.

followups.title: Log handoff
followups.description: add reopen support to a supplied Go worker; prove rotation releases the deleted log.

topics.title: PostgreSQL
topics.tool: A client/server relational database with MVCC, WAL, indexes and replication.
topics.goals: Build depth in transactions, storage, recovery and query behavior; reason about concurrency, retries and durable outcomes. 40-lesson route, with 26 authored.
topics.diagram:
request -> COMMIT -> reply lost
retry   -> operation ID -> existing result

followups.title: Retryable command
followups.description: drop a post-commit response; retry with an operation ID and verify one database effect.

followups.title: Reservation race
followups.description: let two Go clients compete for one item; enforce and check the inventory invariant.

followups.title: Recoverable claim
followups.description: kill a worker after claiming a row; reclaim it and reject results from its stale generation.

topics.title: SQLite
topics.tool: An embedded relational database accessed through local files.
topics.goals: Contrast PostgreSQL with application-owned transactions, single-writer concurrency, WAL/checkpoints and recovery. 32-lesson Essentials proposal.

followups.title: Durable HTTP outbox
followups.description: restart a Go sender after a lost acknowledgment; replay IDs safely to a supplied deduplicating collector.

followups.title: Restartable feed client
followups.description: commit each applied update and cursor together; crash between batches and resume.

followups.title: Writer admission
followups.description: compare two competing writers with a bounded Go gateway to one local SQLite file.

topics.title: Docker / container internals
topics.tool: A container runtime and image workflow built on Linux isolation and resource controls.
topics.goals: Connect writable layers, volumes, process lifetime and limits to application behavior. Skip routine Docker usage; investigate unfamiliar internals.

followups.title: Commit during shutdown
followups.description: terminate the earlier Go/PostgreSQL service during a request; reconcile the client's uncertain result.

followups.title: State after recreation
followups.description: compare a Go service's writable-layer and volume-backed state after container recreation.

topics.title: Networking and application requests
topics.tool: Linux networking plus iproute2, ss, tcpdump, curl, dig, OpenSSL and a small nginx fixture.
topics.goals: Trace DNS, TCP, TLS and HTTP failures; understand deadlines, retries, connection reuse and packet paths.

followups.title: Deadline relay
followups.description: propagate one total deadline through a Go proxy to a delayed upstream; verify cancellation.

followups.title: Retry budget
followups.description: inject lost responses into the earlier operation-ID service; bound attempts and count actual effects.

followups.title: Stale pooled connection
followups.description: restart an upstream; observe a Go client's connection reuse, errors and bounded recovery.

topics.title: nftables
topics.tool: Linux packet filtering, NAT and connection tracking, controlled through nft.
topics.goals: Learn stateful policy and directional failure after routes/veth networks; connect rules to actual request outcomes.

followups.title: One-way partition
followups.description: block replies between two Go peers in owned namespaces; heal and reconcile uncertain requests.

followups.title: Stateful policy change
followups.description: compare an existing Go stream with a new connection after changing filtering rules.

topics.title: Valkey
topics.tool: An in-memory data-structure server, used through valkey-cli and Go clients.
topics.goals: Study expiration, eviction, atomic operations, caching, persistence and replication; decide what can be lost, rebuilt or safely shared.

followups.title: Cache stampede gate
followups.description: coordinate fills across two Go frontends; measure PostgreSQL requests during concurrent misses.

followups.title: Stale-fill race
followups.description: delay an old cache fill; use versions to reject its publication after a newer value.

followups.title: Shared rate limit
followups.description: enforce one atomic request budget across two Go API processes; verify combined admissions.

topics.title: DuckDB
topics.tool: An embedded analytical SQL engine that queries data including Parquet files.
topics.goals: Study columnar execution, scans, pushdown, aggregation, parallelism and spilling; explain analytical work and incomplete results.

followups.title: Two-worker aggregate
followups.description: query two fixed Parquet shards through Go workers; merge sums/counts and reject incomplete results.

followups.title: Import receipt
followups.description: atomically record a batch ID with its imported rows; restart around commit and avoid duplicates.

followups.title: Query admission
followups.description: bound concurrent analytical jobs in a Go wrapper; compare completion and spill evidence.

topics.title: Object storage
topics.tool: Bucket/key object APIs; the current local lab default is SeaweedFS's S3 endpoint.
topics.goals: Study immutable payloads, checksums, retries and manifest publication; separate bulk storage from metadata and rebuildable caches.
topics.diagram:
Go writer -> immutable objects
          -> publish version in PostgreSQL
Go reader -> published version -> DuckDB

followups.title: Manifest publisher
followups.description: upload immutable objects, then advance a PostgreSQL version pointer; interrupt publication and check reader visibility.

followups.title: Retryable chunk upload
followups.description: reuse content-derived IDs after a lost response; verify checksums and one published manifest.

followups.title: Rebuildable cache
followups.description: delete a Go reader's local cache; reconstruct a fixed manifest and verify its dataset with DuckDB.

topics.title: NATS / JetStream
topics.tool: Subject-based messaging; JetStream adds persistent streams, consumers and replay.
topics.goals: Study acknowledgments, redelivery, competing consumers and backlog; separate message delivery from receiver effects.
topics.diagram:
publisher -> stream -> worker -> database effect
                         |
                    acknowledgment

followups.title: Outbox to inbox
followups.description: connect PostgreSQL through Go publishers/consumers; lose acknowledgments and deduplicate receiver effects.

followups.title: Worker crash window
followups.description: crash after a database effect but before acknowledgment; verify safe redelivery to another Go consumer.

followups.title: Slow consumer
followups.description: pause a Go receiver; bound in-flight work and verify every accepted ID after backlog recovery.

topics.title: etcd
topics.tool: A replicated key-value store with revisions, conditional transactions, watches and leases.
topics.goals: Study coordination, quorum, stale ownership and watch recovery; require the protected receiver to enforce fencing.
topics.diagram:
lease -> current owner -> generation token
                             |
                    sink rejects stale writes

followups.title: Fenced owner
followups.description: on takeover, advance the PostgreSQL sink's accepted generation; resume the stale Go worker and reject its writes.

followups.title: Recoverable watcher
followups.description: disconnect a Go watch client; resume by revision or rebuild after compaction and verify convergence.

followups.title: Competing publishers
followups.description: race two Go updates against one expected revision; require the loser to reread before retrying.

topics.title: strace
topics.tool: A CLI tracer for system calls, returned errors and signals.
topics.goals: Use during file, connection and sync investigations; connect syscall evidence to application behavior and recognize tracing limits.

followups.title: Find the blocked hop
followups.description: trace a Go client/worker pair; distinguish blocked reads from connection errors and prove recovery.

followups.title: File publication
followups.description: inspect a Go write/sync/rename sequence; add the missing synchronization call and verify its target.

topics.title: fio
topics.tool: A configurable I/O workload generator with throughput and latency reports.
topics.goals: Use around database storage questions; compare access patterns, queue depth and synchronization with bounded files and workloads.

followups.title: I/O interference
followups.description: use a small Go harness for two bounded fio jobs; vary background concurrency and compare foreground latency.

followups.title: Sync batching
followups.description: compare two fio synchronization settings through a Go wrapper; report latency and completed work.

topics.title: perf
topics.tool: Linux CPU counters and sampled stack profiling, subject to host permissions.
topics.goals: Locate hotspots in familiar workloads; compare useful throughput and latency after one controlled change.

followups.title: Batching tradeoff
followups.description: profile Go peers exchanging fixed records; compare CPU cost and latency before and after batching.

followups.title: Hot routing path
followups.description: profile a supplied Go router; change one hotspot and repeat the same request load.

topics.title: bpftrace
topics.tool: A scripting CLI for dynamic Linux tracing using eBPF probes.
topics.goals: Optional after strace/perf; investigate specific kernel events and latency distributions with scoped filters and measured overhead.

followups.title: Locate the tail
followups.description: correlate a supplied Go service's delayed requests with workload-filtered syscall or scheduler timing.

followups.title: I/O contention probe
followups.description: trace a Go service beside a bounded writer; reduce interference and check useful request progress.

topics.title: Firecracker
topics.tool: A KVM-based microVM monitor controlled through an API.
topics.goals: After Linux isolation, networking and nftables, study guest lifecycle, storage/network boundaries and snapshot behavior using supplied images.
topics.diagram:
host: process + KVM + network
                |
          guest: Go workload

followups.title: Snapshot replay
followups.description: restore a prepared microVM running a Go client; verify repeated operation IDs do not repeat sink effects.

followups.title: Aborted-job cleanup
followups.description: extend a supplied Go launcher; cancel a guest job, reclaim owned resources and launch again successfully.

topics.title: Kubernetes internals
topics.tool: A distributed orchestration/control system exposed through its API and kubectl.
topics.goals: Use disposable kind labs for conflicts, watches, reconciliation, readiness and termination. Study etcd before deep control-plane storage/recovery.

followups.title: Conflicting reconcilers
followups.description: race two Go updates to one ConfigMap; handle resource-version conflicts without losing intended changes.

followups.title: In-flight termination
followups.description: terminate a Pod running the earlier Go operation-ID service; reconcile its outstanding request.

followups.title: Watch interruption
followups.description: disconnect a Go client, relist and resume watching; verify convergence to current object state.

topics.title: Apache Kafka
topics.tool: A partitioned replicated log with producers, offsets and consumer groups.
topics.goals: After NATS, study ordering scope, reassignment, retention and replay; reconcile broker offsets with external effects.

followups.title: Offset/effect crash window
followups.description: store an effect and processed offset in PostgreSQL; crash before broker offset commit and deduplicate replay.

followups.title: Per-key ordering
followups.description: send a tiny keyed dataset from Go producers to two partitions; verify ordering within each key.

followups.title: Consumer reassignment
followups.description: stop one of two Go consumers; verify reassignment and final event-ID coverage.

topics.title: Git internals
topics.tool: A content-addressed object store with commit graphs, refs and packfiles.
topics.goals: Optional storage case study: separate immutable content from mutable publication and understand replica reconstruction.

followups.title: Competing ref publishers
followups.description: race Go wrappers using git update-ref with an expected old ID; verify one publication wins.

followups.title: Lost push acknowledgment
followups.description: interrupt acknowledgment between two owned bare repos; inspect the remote ref before retrying.
